title: Track Joiner
summary: Set the constants of a stunt track so the pieces join with no gap and no corner: continuity and differentiability at a point.
subject: mathematics
learningOutcome: The student can find the constants that make a piecewise function continuous at its joins, and that make it differentiable by matching values and slopes.

levels.title: Close the gap
levels.adds: Baseline: a function is continuous at x = c when the left limit, right limit and value agree, so k comes from one equation (Ex 5.1 Q26 to Q28).
hints: Find the height where the left piece ends at the join.
The right piece must start at the same height: put x = c into it.
Solve that one equation for k.

levels.title: Two joins
levels.adds: Harder: two joins give two equations for two constants a and b (Ex 5.1 Q29, Q30; Examples 10 to 13).
hints: Write the continuity equation at each join.
Each equation has a and b in it. Subtract them.
Then find b from either equation.

levels.title: No corners
levels.adds: New: differentiable at a join needs equal slopes as well as equal values, so match the derivative first (Ex 5.2 Q9, Q10; Misc Q18, Q20).
hints: Differentiate the left piece and put x = c in: that is the slope k must have.
Then match the values to find m.
A track with equal values but different slopes has a corner.

misconceptions: A continuous function is always differentiable
Matching the values at a join is enough for a smooth track
A function can be differentiable where it has a gap
